title: performance canary: enhanced auto-detection of latency regressions + rollout hysteresis
author: Priya Raman
description:
Background: Our continuous performance canary pipeline detects latency/throughput regressions and gates rollouts. We observed two recurring issues: noisy short-term spikes causing false positives, and aggressive automatic traffic shifts when a canary briefly crosses thresholds. This PR introduces (1) an enhanced detection algorithm that blends short- and long-term latency baselines with percentile-based smoothing, and (2) a hysteresis-based rollout guard that requires regression persistence and gradual traffic ramp-back before full rollback.

Changes in this PR: implemented an adaptive detector that maintains EWMA baselines for p50/p95 and a sliding-window percentile for p99; introduced configurable hysteresis parameters (grace_period, persistence_count, rollback_ramp_steps); added integration tests for synthetic spike scenarios; instrumented new metrics and dashboards for visibility.

Why this change: Reduces false positives from transient load spikes, prevents unnecessary rollbacks and oscillation during noisy periods, and gives SREs better visibility into canary behavior. This improves platform reliability and reduces responder fatigue.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector algorithm implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Hysteresis rollout policy implemented and e2e-tested in perf-canary lab
- [x] Metrics + tracing added for debugging (canary.detector.* / canary.rollout.*)
- [x] Documentation updated with parameter guidance and recommended defaults
- [x] Performance impact evaluated — detector adds negligible CPU per canary run

Testing notes: Ran the canary lab on staging with synthetic traffic profiles (steady, transient spike, slow drift). Observed that transient spikes up to 30% over baseline did not trigger rollbacks when shorter than grace_period; sustained regressions (> persistence_count windows) produced deterministic rollback behavior with staged ramping. CI initially had a flaky integration test (timeout) which was fixed by increasing test deadline and adding retry logic.

Related: Linear ENG-8721 (perf canary improvements), ENG-8899 (rollout safety). Linked support ticket SUP-3421 surfaced a customer incident where an aggressive rollback caused a downstream outage — this work addresses the root cause.
